content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Asynchronous Streams with Flow** as part of **Coroutines, Asynchronous Programming, and Concurrency**. Flow represents an asynchronous stream collected from a coroutine; flow operators, cancellation, buffering, and sharing determine behavior. Use the subtopics—The Flow Type, Cold Flows and Collection, Emitting and Transforming Values—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Asynchronous code introduces lifecycle, cancellation, and shared-state concerns. Structured concurrency and explicit data flow make these concerns easier to reason about.

items.title: The Flow Type
items.text: The Flow Type depends on task lifetime and execution context. Keep child tasks inside an owning scope, handle cancellation cooperatively, and avoid unsynchronized shared mutable state.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: A suspend function always runs on a background thread automatically.
